verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The matrix entry agrees term by term — row index i selects the real exponent (a i = α_i, Real.rpow since a : Fin n → ℝ), column index j selects the bump β_j, the integrand is the same product x^{α_i}·β_j(x) against Lebesgue measure, and the paper's m is the Lean n. The one difference is the domain of integration: the Lean definition body at PowerMomentMatrix.lean:253 integrates over all of ℝ (`∫ t, t ^ a i * β j t`), the paper over (0,∞). The rewriting is one step and the repository writes it out: under the standing hypotheses `hsupp : support (β j) ⊆ Icc (l j) (u j)` with `hl : 0 < l j` the integrand vanishes off (0,∞), so `setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero` gives the half-line form; that is exactly SmoothPowerMomentMatrix.lean:120-128, whose statement `D.matrix p i j = ∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ), t ^ D.exponent p i * D.bump p j t` is the paper's display verbatim (Ioi 0 versus the paper's lower limit 0 differs by a null set). Note the half-line form is stated only for the parameterised `Family` wrapper, not as a standalone lemma about `bumpMomentMatrix`; the full-line definition is what every invertibility result is phrased against.
